intro: Judith Bokor’s cello sings above a piano that scarcely stops moving. This little solo from The Carnival of the Animals gives the swan a long, unhurried melody and the water all the work.

sections.label: B · The melody climbs and turns
sections.mNote: Long cello notes over the piano’s running semiquavers

sections.label: C · The cello’s broad phrases
sections.mNote: The piano keeps moving beneath the sustained melody

cues.title: The piano keeps moving
cues.text: The piano sets out G major in flowing broken chords. The cello enters after one bar, with a melody that falls twice before climbing. Six crotchet beats fill each bar; the piano divides them into tiny, even steps beneath the cello’s longer notes.
cues.evidence: Saint-Saëns, Le Cygne, Durand score, plate D.S. 3891, pp. 1–3; cello part edited by Alvin Buechner, Carl Fischer (1907), opening bars. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5f/IMSLP925269-PMLP06099-2024-03-15-12-42-19-01.PDF
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Pavlova gives the swan wings
cues.text: In 1905 Anna Pavlova and the choreographer Michel Fokine turn this cello solo into The Dying Swan. Saint-Saëns’s bird has only twenty-eight bars. On stage, those few minutes become the role most closely associated with Pavlova.
cues.evidence: The ballet’s creation for Pavlova in 1905 is described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_cygne, citing Lynn Garafola, Legacies of Twentieth-Century Dance (2005), pp. 155–156. The Durand score has twenty-eight bars.

cues.title: A long G remains
cues.text: The last phrase slows and the cello comes to rest on a high G, marked pianissimo. The piano keeps its broken chords moving beneath that held note, then finishes alone. Even the final rest carries a pause mark.
cues.evidence: Durand score, plate D.S. 3891, p. 3, last five bars; Carl Fischer cello part (1907), last line. The recording is dated around 1925 in its discography: https://archive.org/details/3-judith-bokor-col-d-17144-fx-16-17-kol-nidrei_202309
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.
